title: The DICTO Yantra: Unique and Traditional, Exact but Not Constructible
description:
Version 7 adds the golden-ratio drawings of Bolton and Macleod (1977) and Fonseca (1986) beside this paper's exact yantras (§14), with the consequence of Wantzel's theorem: the slopes of the DICTO Yantra and of Kulaichev's yantra have degrees 160 and 348, not powers of 2, so neither yantra can be drawn exactly with straightedge and compass; and four references.
Version 6 added nothing to the mathematics: the abstract now opens with the DICTO Yantra's result, Theorem 15 (it is the only Śrī Yantra that meets its conditions, and it has the traditional form), then Theorem 14 with its Lean 4 proof on Palomar; and §1 opens with a summary of what is new.
Version 5 added two uniqueness theorems. Theorem 14: Kulaichev's yantra is the only Śrī Yantra that meets Huet's conditions, Kulaichev's four conditions and admissibility, which answers the uniqueness question Kulaichev asked in 1984, and the list of ways in which that one yantra differs from the traditional form (45 regions, 41 of them triangles, 28 sandhis). Theorem 15: the DICTO Yantra is the only Śrī Yantra that meets Huet's conditions, Kulaichev's (b), (c) and (d), with (d) stated as the incircle of the bindu, the Cleo-Antonius product uv = 2/φ³ in place of (a), and admissibility, and it has the traditional form (43 triangles, 18 marmas, 24 sandhis). Both proofs are computer-assisted (certified computation: exact elimination, certified real roots, ball arithmetic and the Krawczyk test, each with an independent second census). It also adds Chiodo's straightedge-and-compass theorem stated beside Theorem 1 as its predecessor; Theorem 5's uniqueness: exactly one viewpoint centres the yantra, β* = −yH; and, after a full reading of Chapati and Chapati [13], their credits at each point of use: their star-point rule and the parity rule of Proposition 3 pick out the same 43 on every yantra with the traditional pattern but part on Kulaichev's yantra (43 star points, 45 odd regions); with true corners the 74 bounded regions are 53 triangles and 21 four-sided; their observation that the 43 meet only at corners follows from Proposition 3. Version 5 also states that Theorem 14 is proved in Lean 4 by a separate route registered on Palomar [18]; opens the abstract with the point that Kulaichev's own conditions force exactly one figure, and that it is not the traditional yantra; adds §10.3, why nine (Proposition 16); draws the condition breakers (Figure 13); counts E1 on its exact edge as 22 sandhis and two points where four sides meet; reads by free routes the sources Chiodo names for the problem (reference [17]); and, at the first use of the Cleo-Icos, gives its regular name and discoverer, the icosahedron face pyramid (Mackay, 1962) [19].
Version 4 added the credit to G. D. Chapati and R. Chapati (2026) [13], who counted the traditional 43 by another rule (star points of the circuits) and sampled the admissible region numerically.
Version 3 added certificates for Theorems 9 and 10 (irreducibility, real-root isolation, and interval Newton with the elimination identities); certified region counts for the DICTO Yantra (43) and Kulaichev's yantra (45); Appendix H (Theorem 6's relation H in full); a proof-status table (Table 5); admissibility conditions in Theorem 1; the narrower heading of Proposition 8; DICTO's 3-4-5 rhombus yantra as the parallel exact solution beside Kulaichev's (Proposition 12); the crossing that makes Kulaichev's extra triangles and four-sided regions (Figure 12); the rhombus threshold u* where the extra triangles are born (Proposition 13); G1 exactly (degree 152); E1 placed on the edge of that threshold meeting and refined to 90 digits; and the grid figure of §7 is no longer counted as a yantra: Figure 8 ("Why a grid fails") is the evidence for Theorem 7, naming every part outside the circle, and the grid leaves Figure 2; a note on how the exact solutions rank on the traditional regions (§10, §12); a triangles column in Table 3, with each yantra's triangles and four-sided regions shown under its name in Figure 2; Figure 12 and its data (Table 4), so any reader can check the crossing; a certified count for Rh345 (Proposition 12); DICTO's rhombus drawn together as the frame of every result (§3, §12); in §11, which lines of the Cleo sphere run on from yantra to yantra, and why; and "regions" in place of "pieces" throughout, since not every region is a triangle.
Version 2 added the new title; the two exact solutions, the DICTO Yantra (Theorem 9: minimal polynomial of degree 160) and Kulaichev's classical yantra (Theorem 10: degree 348), each checked independently at 260 digits and backwards from the polynomial alone, and their comparison (Proposition 11); overlay figures, each yantra dotted in its own colour over the DICTO Yantra with its shortcomings noted in red, and an overview figure; §13 sorted into closed and exact, computed, and open; and wording: "perfect" is replaced by the conditions it stood for. The subtitle is now “Unique and Traditional, Exact but Not Constructible” (Version 1 to 6: “Two Exact Solutions — Overcoming the Seemingly Impossible, Towards Perfection”).

The DICTO Yantra is the only Śrī Yantra that meets Huet's conditions, Kulaichev's (b), (c) and (d), with (d) stated as the incircle of the bindu, the Cleo-Antonius product uv = 2/φ³ in place of (a), and admissibility, and it has the traditional form: 43 triangles, 18 marmas and 24 sandhis (Theorem 15 and Proposition 11). The proof is computer-assisted, a certified computation: exact divisor lemma and elimination over ℚ(√5), real roots certified by three isolators, ball arithmetic and the Krawczyk test; an independent second census agrees. Kulaichev's own conditions force exactly one figure too, and it is not the traditional yantra: Kulaichev's yantra is the only Śrī Yantra that meets Huet's conditions, Kulaichev's four conditions and admissibility, and it has 45 regions, 41 triangles and 4 four-sided, and 28 sandhis, not 43 triangles and 24 sandhis (Theorem 14, a computer-assisted proof of the same kind). Theorem 14's result is also proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, by a separate, kernel-checked route, registered on Palomar as PALOMAR-2026-11-17-000006. This answers the uniqueness question Kulaichev asked in 1984. Both yantras are solved exactly: the great slopes of the DICTO Yantra on the Cleo-Antonius and of Kulaichev's classical yantra have minimal polynomials of degree 160 and 348 (Theorems 9 and 10). The Śrī Yantra asks its nine triangles to meet three at a time at 18 points (the marmas), to make 43 small triangles, and, in the strict reading, to touch the circle with its smallest top and bottom triangles and to centre the innermost triangle (the bindu). We prove that every rational choice of four natural parameters gives a yantra with all 18 meetings exact in one quadratic field (Theorem 1), and give a yantra with every coordinate in whole-number fractions (Theorem 2). The 43 are the regions lying inside an odd number of the nine triangles (Proposition 3). Spun about its axis the yantra is the axial section of nine nested cones; still tetrahedra show it from three positions narrowed to cos 30° (Proposition 4). The perspectives that keep the circle round keep every meeting and the product of the two great slopes (Theorem 5); in natural coordinates the yantra is one quadratic and one relation of degree 10 (Theorem 6). With one slope for all nine triangles the heights are forced to 2 : 4 : 4 : 4 : 6 : 6 : 8 : 8 : 9 and the great triangles cannot both be inscribed (Theorem 7). The DICTO Yantra, on DICTO's Cleo-Antonius pair (slope product 2/φ³), meets every condition, with 43 triangles, 18 marmas and 24 sandhis; it is the Cleo-Antonius seen from one viewpoint, and its slope u has degree 160 (u² degree 40 over ℚ(√5)). Beside Kulaichev's yantra, DICTO's 3-4-5 rhombus yantra is a parallel exact solution, slope exactly 3/4 and degree 20, meeting every condition but the centred bindu, which it misses by 2.4·10⁻⁵ of the diameter (Proposition 12). Equal great triangles and the Cleo-Antonius are two choices of a fourth condition; the four-parameter family alone does not single out one yantra. The most even exact yantra keeps the 43 but leaves the circle. Every exact yantra found chooses between its small triangles touching the circle and its regions being even: the DICTO Yantra meets every condition of the strict reading, the most even yantra has the most equal regions.

Computation, proofs, verification and drafting with Claude (Anthropic).
